quiz.instructions: Use constant-acceleration models and SI units unless another unit is requested. Give exact answers unless a rounding instruction is stated. Deceleration is a positive magnitude; signed velocity depends on the chosen direction. Where a question has several parts, choose the option with every part correct.

questions.title: 2B Q1
questions.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with constant acceleration \(2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). It passes A at \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and later B, where \(AB=8\) m. Find its speed at B.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 1; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 15; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 20 (Exercise B, Question 1).

questions.title: 2B Q3
questions.prompt: A cyclist travelling at \(12\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) brakes and comes to rest after moving \(36\,\mathrm{m}\) in a straight line. Assuming uniform deceleration, find the deceleration.
questions.working:
Take the initial direction as positive and use \(v^2=u^2+2as\).

\[0=12^2+2a(36),\qquad a=-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}.\]

The deceleration is the positive magnitude \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 3; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 22 (Exercise B, Question 3).

questions.title: 2B Q5
questions.prompt: A particle moves from O towards A along a straight line with constant acceleration \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Its speed at O is \(5.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(OA=20\) m. Find the time taken from O to A.
questions.working:
Use \(s=ut+\frac12at^2\): \(20=5.5t+t^2\).

\[2t^2+11t-40=(2t-5)(t+8)=0.\]

The roots are \(t=2.5\) and \(t=-8\). Reject the negative elapsed time, leaving \(2.5\,\mathrm{s}\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 5; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 24 (Exercise B, Question 5).

questions.title: 2B Q6
questions.prompt: A train accelerates uniformly along a straight horizontal track. It passes two signals at \(54\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\) and \(72\,\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}\); they are \(500\,\mathrm{m}\) apart. Find its acceleration in m/s².
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 6; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 25 (Exercise B, Question 6).

questions.title: 2B Q8
questions.prompt: A particle moves \(38\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(4\,\mathrm{s}\) along a straight line with constant acceleration \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find (a) its initial speed and (b) its final speed.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 8; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 27 (Exercise B, Question 8).

questions.title: 2B Q10
questions.prompt: A stone slides in a straight line across a frozen lake, initially at \(12\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Friction causes constant deceleration \(0.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find (a) the distance before it stops and (b) its speed after travelling half this distance. Give (b) to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
(a) With \(a=-0.8\), \(0=12^2-1.6s\), so \(s=90\,\mathrm{m}\).

(b) Half the distance is \(45\,\mathrm{m}\).

\[v^2=12^2+2(-0.8)(45)=72.\]

Hence the speed is \(\sqrt{72}=8.48528\ldots\approx8.49\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) (3 s.f.). It is not half the initial speed.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 10; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 29 (Exercise B, Question 10).

questions.title: 2B Q12
questions.prompt: A particle moves horizontally with constant acceleration \(-2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\), taking AB as positive. At \(t=0\) it passes A at \(12\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\); \(AB=32\) m. The acceleration remains constant after it reverses direction. Find (a) both times it is at B and (b) the corresponding signed velocities, in the same order.
questions.working:
(a) Use \(s=ut+\frac12at^2\): \(32=12t-t^2\).

\[(t-4)(t-8)=0,\qquad t=4\,\mathrm{s}\text{ or }8\,\mathrm{s}.\]

(b) \(v=12-2t\), so the velocities are \(+4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at \(t=4\) and \(-4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) at \(t=8\). The second crossing is on the return journey.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 12; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 31 (Exercise B, Question 12).

questions.title: 2B Q14
questions.prompt: A particle P passes the origin at \(t=0\) with velocity \(+14\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and constant acceleration \(-4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Point A has coordinate \(x=22.5\) m. Find (a) the difference between the two times P passes A and (b) the total distance travelled between these crossings.
questions.working:
(a) \(22.5=14t-2t^2\), so

\[(2t-5)(2t-9)=0.\]

The crossing times are \(2.5\) and \(4.5\,\mathrm{s}\), a difference of \(2\,\mathrm{s}\).

(b) The turning time is \(14/4=3.5\,\mathrm{s}\). Its coordinate then is \(14(3.5)-2(3.5)^2=24.5\,\mathrm{m}\).

The distance out and back is \(2(24.5-22.5)=4\,\mathrm{m}\), although net displacement is zero.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 14; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 17; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 33 (Exercise B, Question 14).

questions.title: 2B Q15
questions.prompt: A car moves forwards along a straight horizontal road with constant acceleration, passing consecutive points A, B and C. \(AB=100\) m, \(BC=300\) m, and its speeds at B and C are \(14\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find (a) its acceleration and (b) the time from A to C, giving (b) to 3 significant figures.
questions.working:
(a) On BC, \(20^2=14^2+2a(300)\), giving \(a=0.34\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).

(b) The distance AC is \(400\,\mathrm{m}\). Hence \(20^2=u_A^2+2(0.34)(400)\), so \(u_A^2=128\).

The car is moving forwards, so \(u_A=\sqrt{128}=8\sqrt2\), not the negative square root.

\[t=\frac{20-8\sqrt2}{0.34}.\]

This is \(25.5479\ldots\,\mathrm{s}\), so \(t=25.5\,\mathrm{s}\) (3 s.f.). Keep unrounded values until the final step.
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 15; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 17; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF page 34 (Exercise B, Question 15).

questions.title: 2B Q16
questions.prompt: P and Q move along the same straight horizontal line with constant accelerations \(2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\) and \(3.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). P passes A at \(t=0\) at \(4\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). One second later Q passes A at \(3\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), in the same direction. For \(t\geq1\), find (a) their displacements from A as functions of t, (b) when they meet, measured from P passing A, and (c) the distance of the meeting point from A.
questions.working:
(a) Measure displacement in the common forward direction. P has travelled for \(t\) seconds; Q has travelled for \(t-1\) seconds since passing A.

\[s_P=4t+t^2.\]

\[s_Q=3(t-1)+1.8(t-1)^2.\]

(b) Set \(s_P=s_Q\) and simplify: \(0.8t^2-4.6t-1.2=0\).

\[4t^2-23t-6=(t-6)(4t+1)=0.\]

Reject \(t=-\frac14\); the applicable meeting time is \(6\,\mathrm{s}\), measured from P passing A (5 s after Q passes A).

(c) \(s_P=4(6)+6^2=60\,\mathrm{m}\).
questions.source_ref: M1, Exercise 2B, Question 16; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/M1 chapter 1 exercises.pdf, PDF page 17; Source Files/2iec/Mechanics Chapt 01 SUVAT/Solutions chapter 01.pdf, PDF pages 35–36 (Exercise B, Question 16).
